jobs.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one panoramic 3:1 facility illustration for a football-management game. Create a NEW scene, not a UI. Image 1 is a STYLE reference, not a request to copy its football stadium into other kinds of room. Match its painted Western sports-comic treatment, hand-crafted detail, foliage/material rendering and late-afternoon warmth. If another reference is supplied it establishes the facility layout/camera. Output one complete horizontal wide illustration around 1920x640, with no border, labels, letters, numbers, logos, branding, speech balloons, watermarks or embedded UI. No people, faces, vehicles or fabricated statistics. Keep image composition usable in a narrow panoramic UI slot, with the main architecture and important equipment in the central horizontal band. Preserve natural proportions and believable football architecture. Forest/stadium greens harmonize with #264532, with warm brick, timber, cream and blue-grey sky, not monochrome green. Contemporary Western painted sports comic / graphic novel background: expressive rough brush inking, layered opaque gouache colour, tactile wood/brick/grass/fabric, textured edges, selective graphic highlights, warm natural light and nuanced shadows. Match the supplied approved stadium reference closely in brushwork, palette and level of crafted detail. Richly rendered and immersive, not flat vector art, pixel art, photorealism or a 3D render. Scene: Football stadium, low sideline viewpoint across grass toward the opposite stand, a near goal/net toward one edge, believable pitch markings and warm sky. Do not turn this into an aerial schematic. Use the layout reference only for the camera and the pitch position; the stands are rebuilt to a much larger scale. A rebuilt, very large, fully enclosed bowl with a continuous roofline falling from the corners to the centre, four tiers of seating on the long sides, deep terraces at the ends, a broad landmark roof on steel trusses and tall floodlight masts above it, built in weathered brick, painted timber and steel. It is the largest ground drawn so far, a new landmark bowl, communicated through architecture only. Period: English football facilities in 1950-1969: weathered brick, timber, corrugated roofs, steel posts, standing terraces, hand-maintained turf and traditional equipment. No LED panels, digital screens, plastic seat mosaics, futuristic roofs or modern sports-science technology. This is completed facility stage 9; communicate its scale through architecture only, with no stage number or capacity drawn in the image.
